analysis: Examined three provider-swift changes. (1) WholeMacServiceBudget.swift adds isIdle(for:), performIfIdle(for:_:) and a private isIdleLocked helper (lines ~227-247). They are read-only checks over the existing charges/unboundedActivities/idleSince state, taken under the same lock. performIfIdle runs a caller body while holding the NSLock. The body must not reenter the budget, which is documented; the body and its callers are not in the supplied evidence, so deadlock risk is unverified. No new exposure of prompts, keys or attestation material. (2) ProviderLoop+NemotronSuperAdmission.swift: the load gate now releases retained KV segments and the buffer pool once (releaseReclaimableMemoryForLoad) before evicting idle models. nemotronSuperLoadIsCertainToFail becomes async and refactors the room check into nemotronSuperRoomReaches. Inspected the eviction loop, which is bounded: poolDropped is set once, and declined evictions are capped at 3. This is memory-admission logic for local availability only (T-029 and T-028 adjacent). Releasing buffer-pool memory arguably reduces residual-data lifetime. No authorization, encryption or attestation path is touched. Integration questions: callers of nemotronSuperLoadIsCertainToFail must now await, and must re-check request verdicts after the suspension, as the comment says. Those callers, the definitions of releaseReclaimableMemoryForLoad, reclaimableMemoryBytes(from:countingRetainedKVSegments:) and GlobalKVCacheBudget.busyEnginesKeepReclaimableMemory(), and the other call sites of performIfIdle (for example the SSD prefix-cache maintenance) are outside the supplied evidence. (3) ProviderLoop+Capacity.swift is a comment-only change. No threat-model assets or boundaries (TB-002, TB-007, T-041) are weakened by the supplied hunks. A caller-side reentrancy or cancellation race remains unverified.
